title: Join the Webinar “Climate Change and Spatial Planning on the Baltic Sea Coast: Where Are We Now?”
content:
PA Spatial Planning invites to join the webinar “Climate Change and Spatial Planning on the Baltic Sea Coast: Where Are We Now?” on 3 December 2026 online 9:30–12:30 CET. Organised within the Baltic PlaNet project platform, this event launches an online webinar series designed to support spatial planners in addressing climate change risks in their work, foster exchange of experience and strengthen cooperation among planners across the Baltic Sea Region, contributing to more climate-resilient Baltic Sea coasts.

As the first in a series of Baltic PlaNet webinars, this webinar will focus on basics of climate science, introducing with observed climate trends and the impacts of climate change in the Baltic Sea Region. This will be followed by short presentations from spatial planners working in coastal areas across the Baltic Sea Region, sharing their observations and experiences of how climate change is affecting coastal areas, what challenges it creates, and how these are (or should be) addressed through spatial planning and coastal management.

title: Baltic Sea Tourism Forum 2026: Turning ideas into action for the future of tourism
content:
The Baltic Sea Tourism Forum 2026 brought tourism professionals from across the Baltic Sea Region to Helsingør, Denmark, on 2–3 November to exchange ideas, share practical solutions and discuss how tourism can become more sustainable, resilient and beneficial for the places where it takes place. This year’s Forum focused on four themes: changing tourism behaviour at scale, making cross-border rail tourism work, spreading the benefits of cruise tourism beyond the biggest ports, and exploring the future of tourism.

Photo: Emil Hornstrup Jakobsen / Fotoemil.nu

A recurring question throughout the Forum was how to turn sustainability ambitions into choices and actions that work in practice.
The discussions showed that meaningful change requires both scale and solutions that make sustainable choices easy and attractive for visitors. Examples from destinations around the Baltic Sea demonstrated how this can be done in different ways.

title: Interreg Baltic Sea Region programme continues the dialogue with the Strategy on future transnational cooperation
content:
What should Interreg Baltic Sea Region, as a transnational cooperation programme, address after 2027? As work on the future Programme progresses, dialogue with regional stakeholders help further develop the cooperation needs identified by the Programme countries. The EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region is of particular importance in this process, bringing the macro-regional strategic perspective and helping to ensure that future cooperation needs are firmly rooted in the updated Action Plan and its implementation.

The Baltic Sea region is changing – and so are the challenges that cooperation needs to address. Security and resilience have gained urgency; climate impacts are becoming increasingly tangible; and demographic, green, and digital transitions are reshaping our territories and economies.

title: Four new Baltic Sea Region Cultural Pearls selected to strengthen social resilience in 2027
content:
The BSR Cultural Pearls Network is growing. Following a selection process that began in March, Gjøvik/Norway, Šilutė/Lithuania, Rēzekne/Latvia, and Hel/Poland have been selected as BSR Cultural Pearls 2027. These cities will continue their work towards strengthening social resilience through culture in their communities, starting from grassroot-level steps towards sustainable solutions.

Their selection emerged from a strong field of 13 candidates, demonstrating the interest among municipalities across the Baltic Sea Region in using culture to bring communities together and shape more resilient places.

title: Cycling Connects: Bringing Tourism and Transport Together for a More Connected Baltic Sea Region
content:
Almost 80 participants joined the “Cycling Connects” webinar on 26 October 2026, marking the first jointly organised thematic event by the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR) Policy Areas Tourism and Transport. The strong interest and lively exchange confirmed that cycling tourism is much more than a tourism product – it is an important link between sustainable mobility, regional development and cross-border cooperation.

The webinar brought together representatives of the European Commission, European cycling organisations, regional authorities, tourism stakeholders and EU-funded projects to exchange perspectives, showcase practical initiatives and explore how closer cooperation between tourism and transport can support a more sustainable and accessible Baltic Sea Region.

Cycling tourism is growing in importance across Europe, offering opportunities to encourage low-carbon travel, connect urban and rural destinations, support local businesses and develop attractive cross-border tourism experiences. Yet unlocking its full potential requires cooperation across sectors, administrative borders and policy areas.

title: Baltic Sea Region mental health work presented at the WHO Regional Committee for Europe
content:
The approach of the Baltic Sea Region Mental Health Platform was presented to health ministers and delegates of the 53 Member States of the WHO European Region at the 76th session of the WHO Regional Committee for Europe (RC76), held in Copenhagen on 27-29 October 2026. Ülla-Karin Nurm, Director of the NDPHS Secretariat, which leads the platform and coordinates Policy Area Health in the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region, took the floor under three agenda items.

A session with mental health on the agenda

The Regional Committee is WHO’s decision-making body in the European Region and sets the direction for regional health policy. This year, Member States adopted “Ageing is living”, the regional strategy on healthy ageing for 2026-2030. They were also consulted on a new strategy to tackle noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and advance well-being through health promotion, due for adoption in 2027. WHO/Europe also raised the possibility of a complementary regional strategy on mental health and well-being for the same period, which is still under discussion. The consultation comes 40 years after the Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion.

title: Watch: stronger eastern border regions through cooperation
content:
A new documentary follows Europe’s eastern border regions as they turn shared geopolitical challenges into practical ideas, stronger partnerships and more resilient communities through interregional cooperation.

The 12-minute documentary ‘Stronger eastern border regions: the Regio-Silience’ journey follows two years of collaboration among more than 30 local and regional authorities from Poland, the Baltic States, Finland and Norway. 

Supported by the Interreg Europe Policy Learning Platform, Regio-Silience brings regions together to exchange experience and explore practical responses in economic development, security, community resilience and regional cooperation. The film shows the journey from Antwerp to policy-learning activities in Olsztyn, Salla and Kirkenes. 

The documentary also shows how regional experience can inform the European debate on the future of the EU’s eastern border regions. It highlights the value of peer learning and cooperation in developing practical ideas, building lasting partnerships and strengthening resilience.

title: Building bridges to adulthood: PA Education shares School to Work experience in Brussels
content:
How can local and regional actors provide more coordinated support to vulnerable young people as they move into adulthood? This question was at the centre of a workshop held on 14 October 2026 during the European Week of Regions and Cities in Brussels.

The workshop, No child left behind: building bridges to adulthood, was organised by the European Commission, Directorate-General for Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion (DG EMPL), together with Eurocities. Around 50 participants gathered to discuss how young people can receive more continuous and coordinated support when transitioning between education, employment and social services.

Anders Bergström, Policy Area Coordinator for Education under the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR), participated as a panellist, sharing experiences from the flagship School to Work (S2W).

title: Youth Democracy Festivals empower youth as the future of democracy
content:
Through D-Effect project, young people across the Baltic Sea Region co-create Youth Democracy Festivals, strengthening civic participation, democratic skills and cooperation between youth and decision-makers.

Young people are often invited to discuss democracy, but rarely have a real opportunity to shape it. The Interreg South Baltic project D-Effect is changing this approach by giving youth an active role in designing and delivering democratic initiatives within their communities.

Implemented by partners from Poland, Sweden, Denmark, Germany and Lithuania, D-Effect promotes civic engagement through a practical methodology built around Round Tables, Youth Democracy Festivals (YDF) and direct dialogue with decision-makers. Rather than being passive participants, young people become co-creators of activities that address local challenges and strengthen democratic culture.

title: Three new EU funded projects – one shared mission: Boosting Rural Circular Bioeconomy
content:
In autumn 2026, three Interreg Baltic Sea Region projects – CircularFarmPlastics, Rural Symbiosis and BioGold – are launching with a shared mission: to boost circular bioeconomy in rural areas by turning side streams, residues and difficult waste streams into new value, stronger cooperation and practical business opportunities.

The BioBoosters Network is hosting an open launch webinar for three projects advancing the rural circular bioeconomy in the Baltic Sea Region: BioGold, CircularFarmPlastics and Rural Symbiosis. The event will introduce their activities and explore opportunities for cooperation with the project teams. The webinar is particularly relevant to farmers, biogas producers, rural businesses, waste collection and recycling companies, regional and local authorities, researchers, and business support organisations interested in practical circular bioeconomy solutions.
